links.outcome: LLM-generated lymphoma report accuracy and hallucination of newly involved sites
links.effect: Neither model hallucinated new nodal/extranodal sites; nodal accuracy 0.99 vs 0.97; Lugano stage accuracy 0.85 (Llama 4) vs 0.60 (Llama 3.3); treatment response 0.88 vs 0.65.
links.quote: Neither model produced hallucinations of newly involved nodal or extranodal sites.

links.outcome: Head-to-head comparison of two candidate LLMs on same data for report generation
links.effect: Llama-4-Scout was significantly more accurate than Llama-3.3-70B for nodal (0.99 vs 0.97, p<0.001), stage (0.85 vs 0.60) and treatment response (0.88 vs 0.65).
links.quote: This difference was more pronounced when predicting Lugano stage and treatment response (stage: 0.85 [95% CI = 0.79-0.89] vs. 0.60 [95% CI = 0.53-0.67], p < 0.001; treatment response: 0.88 [95% CI = 0.83-0.92] vs. 0.65 [95% CI = 0.58-0.71], p < 0.001).

unlisted_practices: Locally deployed open-weight LLMs for privacy-preserving processing of clinical reports
Chain-of-thought prompting to generate structured reports

screen.reason: The study retrospectively evaluates the performance and accuracy of two locally deployed LLMs (Llama 3.3 and Llama 4) for generating structured lymphoma reports using chain-of-thought prompting, but does not test or compare a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
